title: Plutonium Half-Life Decay
learningObjectives: Explain that half-life is the time required to lose half of radioactivity.
Compare decay rates of plutonium isotopes with different half-lives.
Describe how decay transforms plutonium into daughter products that can remain radioactive.

evidence.quote: The different isotopes have different “half-lives” – the time it takes to lose half of its radioactivity.

explanations.text: Half-life is the time it takes for a radioactive material to lose half of its radioactivity.

evidence.quote: Pu-239 has a half-life of 24,100 years and Pu-241’s half-life is 14.4 years.
Substances with shorter half-lives decay more quickly than those with longer half-lives, so they emit more energetic radioactivity.

explanations.text: Isotopes with shorter half-lives decay more quickly. Pu-241 decays faster than Pu-239 because its half-life is much shorter.

evidence.quote: Like any radioactive isotopes, plutonium isotopes transform when they decay.
Many of these “daughter products” are themselves radioactive.

explanations.text: Plutonium isotopes transform when they decay into different isotopes or elements, many of which remain radioactive.

predictions.prompt: A 100-gram sample has a half-life of 5 years. How much remains after 5 years?
A 200-gram sample has a half-life of 10 years. How much remains after 20 years?
